title: Running through July 11th only, at HERE Arts Center via Colt Coeur #t...
transcript: It's a devastating will-they-won’t-they queer saga taking place in the same tent over many years. In this play, Camping, we first meet Ari and Britt as they're about to lose their virginities to a boy on his way to the tent. We follow them to Girl Scout camp, a music festival and so on into adulthood. All the while they're kind of bumping up against the line between best friends and something more. Some people might find it painfully relatable, but even as someone who didn't, I thought it was an illuminating, gripping and fully-realized piece of drama. The tent concept is such a clever theatrical device and an evocative central image as this place for escape and intimacy. And I was maybe equally impressed by the direction from Adrienne Campbell-Holt and the acting from Alice Kremelberg and Colby Minifie. As much as I genuinely really liked the script from Victoria Lynne Barclay, I can also easily imagine a production of it that kind of crumbles if you don't perfectly calibrate the sexuaI and romantic tension simmering under the surface and bubbling up in just the right moments and to just the right extent. And from an acting perspective, capturing the love and chemistry between these characters, but also the deep turmoil within them. On that note, I also want to shout out the intimacy direction from Safwa Ozair and Megan Carver, which is maybe some of the best I've ever seen. They make it feel so primal and messy and impulsive, but so specific, where just the tiniest details, like the placement of a hand or the exact duration of time that a contact lasts, completely changes the story being told in that moment. I think all of the writing and production elements came together most strikingly in a scene taking place at a music festival. There's this emotionally shattering monologue that's gonna become an audition staple as soon as it's published, followed by this extremely charged moment of physical intimacy that's just burned into my brain. Meanwhile, the r lights and electronic dance music are, kind of pulsing melancholically just outside the tent. Absolutely going down is one of my favourite scenes of the year, which kind of leads to my one issue with the play: I think it peaks halfway through and afterward starts to tread water a little bit and the in-story justifications for taking place in the tent get less organic. But honestly, I was still so invested that it really didn't bother me that much.
classificationReason: Creator shares first-hand opinions about the script, direction (Adrienne Campbell-Holt), and performances (Alice Kremelberg, Colby Minifie) of this Off-Broadway production at HERE Arts Center, clearly having attended the show.
